sections.title: Sound of letter y
paragraphs: The name of this letter is (ы) /ɨ/. Its main sound appears in (сын) /sɨn/, which means son. This letter makes two sounds in Russian. It is a vowel, which is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. It never appears at the start of a native Russian word.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Pull your tongue back slightly toward the middle of your mouth. Keep the middle of the tongue high. Spread your lips wide and keep them flat. Let the air flow freely while your voice vibrates. For the weaker sound, lower your tongue slightly and relax your mouth. Place a finger across your lips to make sure they do not round.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: In stressed syllables after hard consonants, you say the main sound, as in (дым) /dɨm/. A stressed syllable is a syllable that you say with more strength. In unstressed syllables, the sound becomes slightly lower and shorter, as in (рыбак) /rɨ̞ˈbak/. The letter always follows a non-palatalized consonant.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not say the sound like the vowel in seen. That sound pushes your tongue too far forward. Do not say it like the vowel in soon, because your lips must not round. Think of the vowel in roses. Keep your lips spread and pull your tongue back into the centre of your mouth.
